questions.prompt: A designer sizes an axis with T_M = (T_L + T_a) x S_f and is unsure about the payload mass and the friction. Where should the extra caution go?
options: Into every input: heavier mass, lower efficiency and higher friction, then S_f as well.
Into the single safety factor S_f applied once to the torque, with the other inputs at honest values.
Nowhere: a datasheet rated torque already contains all margins.
Into the supply voltage, by choosing the highest available.
questions.explanation: Padding several inputs and then applying S_f stacks the factors silently, so the real margin becomes unknown. Keep inputs honest (or at a stated pessimistic end of a known range) and apply S_f once on the torque.

questions.prompt: A 6 kg robot with two driven wheels of radius 0.05 m drives at constant speed on level ground with a rolling-resistance coefficient of 0.02. Torque per wheel in N m. Precision 0.002.
A move of 1.2 m has a speed limit of 0.6 m/s and an acceleration limit of 0.6 m/s^2 (trapezoidal profile). Total time in seconds. Precision 0.02.
A load inertia of 3 kg cm^2 is driven through a 4:1 gearbox by a motor with rotor inertia 0.05 kg cm^2. Inertia ratio J_L / (J_0 i^2). Precision 0.02.
A servo passes the peak-torque check, but its torque over a repeating cycle is high. Which quantity decides whether it overheats?
options: The peak torque, compared with the stall torque.
The RMS torque over the whole cycle including the rest, compared with the rated torque.
The average speed, compared with the no-load speed.
The supply voltage, compared with the rated voltage.
questions.explanation: Winding heat is R x I^2, so the thermal limit applies to the root-mean-square torque (current) over the cycle, with the rest time counted in the cycle time.

questions.prompt: A screw of lead 4 mm and efficiency 0.5 must push a 100 N load. Motor torque in N m. Precision 0.003.
A brushed motor at 12 V has a stall current of 6 A and runs at 1.5 A. The driver is rated 3 A continuous and 5 A peak. What is the correct verdict?
options: Pass: 1.5 A is below the 3 A continuous rating.
Pass: 6 A is close enough to 5 A peak.
Not safe: the stall current exceeds the peak rating, so add a current limit and stall detection or use a larger driver.
Fail only if the supply voltage is above 24 V.
questions.explanation: A jammed shaft draws V/R, here 6 A, above the 5 A peak. The running current is fine, but the stall case needs a current limit, stall detection or a bigger driver.

questions.prompt: A small arm must lift a 0.2 kg payload at the end of a 0.5 m link through 90 degrees in 1.5 s. Describe the sizing steps you would follow to choose a motor, a gear ratio and a driver, and name the checks that could reject your first choice.
rubric: Computes the gravity torque at the worst (horizontal) pose and the acceleration torque J times alpha from a trapezoidal profile, then applies a safety factor once.
Checks peak torque against the motor capability, RMS torque over the cycle against the rated torque, and the speed left at the working torque.
Checks driver current (continuous and stall), voltage headroom against back-EMF, and chooses feedback (resolution at the output, backlash).
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
